case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread (October–November 2025) covers the full lifecycle of Sony's FY26 TV Bluetooth SIG certification, from profile test execution through final Qualification Workspace submission. The product is a Sony TV (consumer electronics) registering A2DP (v1.4) and AVRCP (v1.6.2) profiles. The registration strategy uses QDID 199247 (FY23 prior product) Include to inherit A2DP/AVRCP ICS at the profile level, combined with current Host DN (Q346069) and Controller DN (Q333791) Includes — minimizing the profile test burden to only the version-delta items. The thread covers seven distinct consulting Q&As: (1) multiple PTS version reports as valid SIG evidence for version-regression items; (2) correct PTS report format (Generate Report 'Report_AVRCP_' vs. raw log 'TestReport_'); (3) Test Case Category D items are not required (不問); (4) Qualification Workspace layer-to-QDID assignment for multi-QDID Include setup; (5) AVRCP ICS version mismatch in PTS report (v1.5 → regenerate as v1.6.2); (6) Compliance Folder requirements post-July 2024 (mandatory for all registrations, wireless module block diagram acceptable, not required before SIG Submission); (7) 'Allow Others to Include' setting = No restricts external company Include access. The thread also covers AVRCP test execution difficulties on Android TV (Google Play Music required, ADB commands for APK install and MP3 push), ICS 1/8 NO to remove Suspend test when product doesn't support it, and the 11/5 Pass deadline for 11/9 registration. The thread concludes with all Submission Status items green in the Review page and the customer being asked for final confirmation to proceed.
all_questions_found: Can we submit split PTS reports from two different PTS versions (one item on old version, rest on new version) as SIG evidence?
The TestReport_ XML file we submitted — is this valid SIG qualification evidence?
A2DP/SRC/SYN is non-Pass but Test Case Category is D — is A2DP still considered passed?
The TV doesn't implement Suspend — can we change A2DP ICS 1/8 to NO mid-test to remove the SUS test case?
For the multi-QDID Include registration (199247 + Q346069 + Q333791), which QDID do we assign to each layer? Is Option 2b correct? Is TCRL pkg100 correct?
Our AVRCP PTS report shows ICS Version 1.5 but our target is 1.6.2. How do we fix this — do we need to re-run the test?
We don't recall ever needing a Compliance Folder before. Is this a new July 2024 requirement? Can we use the wireless module block diagram? When is it needed?
If 'Allow Others to Include' is set to No, can our own company still Include the QDID while external companies cannot?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Three procedural clusters define this thread: (1) PTS evidence quality: two common mistakes emerged — submitting raw logs (TestReport_) instead of Generate Report output (Report_AVRCP_), and having AVRCP ICS version set to 1.5 instead of 1.6.2 in PTS before generating the report. Additionally, a PTS tool regression caused one AVRCP test item to pass only on an older ETS version — the SIG allows split multi-version reports as valid evidence. (2) Registration strategy and ICS: the profile test exemption via QDID 199247 Include is the central strategy — Profile layers inherit A2DP/AVRCP ICS from the FY23 product, Host layers from Q346069, Controller from Q333791, RF/RF_PHY from Q333791 (to align with reused RF reports). Category D items are explicitly not required. A2DP ICS 1/8 NO correctly removes Suspend test scope when the product doesn't implement Suspend. (3) Post-July 2024 administration: Compliance Folder is now mandatory for all registrations (not just Design), with document scope simplified for TV (wireless module block diagram instead of full TV system), and assembly timing is after submission. The 'Allow Others to Include' setting controls whether external companies can reference the QDID in their own registrations.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: For PTS evidence: always use Generate Report (Report_AVRCP_); split reports across PTS versions are acceptable when a tool regression prevents passing on the latest version. For AVRCP ICS version in the report: correct it by changing the PTS ICS setting and regenerating the Report file — no retest needed. For ICS scope: Category D = not required; features the product doesn't support should be removed from ICS (changing ICS is correct, not a workaround). For Qualification Workspace layer assignment: Profile→prior QDID, Host→Host DN, Controller+RF→Controller DN; Option 2b; TCRL pkg100.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting TestReport_ files instead of Report_AVRCP_ files will be rejected by the Qualification Workspace. Submitting a PTS report with AVRCP v1.5 when v1.6.2 is required will cause a version mismatch. Misassigning QDID layers in the multi-Include setup will break ICS inheritance and generate full profile test requirements. Failing to prepare the Compliance Folder (now mandatory post-July 2024) will leave the registration non-compliant.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For TV (Android TV) A2DP/AVRCP certifications: (1) Brief the customer on PTS evidence format before testing — Generate Report only, check ICS version before generating; (2) Proactively explain that split multi-PTS-version reports are allowed for regression items — this avoids unnecessary escalation when the chip vendor reports a tool issue; (3) For any customer who last registered pre-July 2024, explain the Compliance Folder requirement upfront and what documents are needed (operation manual BT section, wireless module block diagram, product outline drawing, antenna data sheet with gain characteristics); (4) For multi-QDID Include registrations with profile ICS inheritance, document the exact layer-to-QDID assignment in the registration plan before starting — the RF/RF_PHY assignment to the Controller DN (not the prior product QDID) is a common source of confusion; (5) When a product doesn't implement a Bluetooth feature (e.g., Suspend), proactively check ICS before testing rather than discovering it mid-test.
